page: Amazon Web Services c9gd.metal-48xl is a bare-metal compute-optimized server instance built on 64-bit Arm architecture with AWS Graviton processors. It features 192 dedicated physical CPU cores running at a clock frequency of 3.3 GHz without multithreading, resulting in 192 virtual CPUs. The instance is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per CPU core. Additionally, it integrates 11,400 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage directly attached as instance store volumes, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps. It does not include discrete GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The bare-metal configuration eliminates hypervisor overhead, granting direct access to the underlying Graviton processor hardware and NVMe storage drives. Featuring a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, this server optimizes compute-bound parallel processing and execution density. High qualitative cost efficiency is achieved through the energy-efficient Arm processor design combined with integrated NVMe storage, reducing reliance on separate block storage attachments. A primary technical tradeoff is the non-persistent nature of instance store storage, which requires application-level data redundancy. The c9gd.metal-48xl is structured for parallel compute processing, distributed data analytics, high-throughput batch operations, and latency-sensitive databases requiring fast local I/O.
description: Amazon Web Services c9gd.metal-48xl is a bare-metal compute-optimized instance powered by 192 physical cores on custom 64-bit Arm-based AWS Graviton processors operating at 3.3 GHz. Configured with a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the system includes 384.0 GB of system memory and 11,400 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD local storage. It delivers a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and operates without hypervisor overhead. The high core count combined with high-speed local instance store volumes provides operational cost efficiency for compute-intensive and I/O-heavy workloads without requiring dedicated external storage systems. However, ephemeral local storage necessitates software-level data persistence management. This instance is best suited for compute-bound parallel processing, distributed data analytics, high-throughput batch jobs, and performance-critical database engine deployments.
